paragraphs: Skedda sells booking software for shared workplace space, giving staff self-serve booking of desks, rooms and other resources. The company frames it as one platform to book space and manage operations, backed by data about how the square footage is used.

People browse desks by neighborhood on an interactive floor plan and see where colleagues are sitting. A desk takes three clicks to reserve from a desktop, a phone or Microsoft Teams. Check-in by QR code or automatic Wi-Fi connection frees desks that nobody claims. Administrators set approvals, quotas, priority windows and check-in rules that govern when and where people book. Room bookings sync with Outlook or Google calendar events, and release automatically when the calendar event is declined. Reporting covers desk and room usage, peak hours and booking patterns over time.

The company says it has 8,000 global customers across 28 countries and 3m active users. For campuses it describes cleaning buffers between sessions and approval workflows for spaces in high demand. Customers named on the desk booking page include Toyota Connected EU, PVH Corp, Columbia University, Aon, and Pella Windows & Doors. The site states SOC 2 Type 2 certification with independently audited controls. It also states GDPR compliance, with data processing agreements available.

quote.text: Skedda replaces the daily scramble of calendar conflicts, room hoarding, and manual admin with a conference room booking system that runs itself.
